back: mRNA → cDNA (reverse transcriptase) → into plasmid (restriction enzyme, ligase) → transform E. coli → select → ferment → purify.

front: Why use cDNA rather than genomic DNA?
back: cDNA has no introns; bacteria cannot splice RNA.
Identical to human (fewer immune reactions), plentiful supply, pure and consistent, ethically and religiously acceptable.

front: How does animal insulin differ from human insulin?
back: Pig: one amino acid different; cattle: three.
A protein made by an organism from a gene transferred into it by genetic engineering.
Clotting protein for haemophilia A, made in mammalian cell culture; avoids viruses from donated blood.
Enzyme replacement for ADA deficiency (a form of SCID), where toxic products kill lymphocytes.

front: Why use mammalian or yeast cells for some proteins?
back: Eukaryotic cells have ER and Golgi to add carbohydrate groups and fold proteins correctly.
Extraction and purification of a product from a culture after fermentation.
